name: budget_50
prompt: I have $50 to spend at the store. What should I buy, and what are 2 recipes I can make with it?
pass_if: search_recipes is called before any search_prices call
Exactly 2 recipes are recommended
search_prices is called only for non-staple ingredients of those 2 recipes
estimate_basket is called with budget 50 and the final basket has within_budget true
Every non-staple ingredient of both recipes is on the shopping list
Weight items are in the basket with pounds and shown as pounds at a price per pound

name: tight_budget_15
prompt: I only have $15 for groceries this week. Give me one dinner recipe and a shopping list.
pass_if: estimate_basket is called with budget 15
The final basket has within_budget true, or the agent clearly says it cannot fit and offers a cheaper option
No total above $15 is presented as fitting the budget
Every non-staple ingredient of the recipe is on the shopping list

name: have_ingredients
prompt: I have chicken, rice and garlic at home. What can I make, and what would the rest of the ingredients cost?
pass_if: search_recipes is called with chicken, rice and garlic as ingredients
chicken, rice and garlic are NOT priced, since the user has them
The recipe's other non-staple ingredients are priced and totaled with estimate_basket
No budget is invented

name: peanut_allergy
prompt: I'm allergic to peanuts. I have chicken and coconut milk. What Thai dish can I make?
pass_if: No recommended recipe contains peanuts or a peanut product (check the full ingredient list)
The agent acknowledges the allergy
If an ingredient's safety is uncertain (for example curry paste), the agent says so instead of guessing

name: vegetarian
prompt: I'm vegetarian. Suggest 2 recipes I can make for under $30 and tell me what to buy.
pass_if: No recommended recipe contains meat, fish, or meat-based stock (chicken stock and fish sauce count)
The agent checks ingredients rather than trusting the category: 9 of the 100 recipes TheMealDB labels Vegetarian contain meat, stock or fish sauce
estimate_basket is called with budget 30 and the final basket has within_budget true
Exactly 2 recipes are recommended

name: memory_followup
turns: I have $40 to spend. Give me 1 dinner recipe and a shopping list.
pass_if: Turn 2 keeps the $40 budget without being told again (estimate_basket is called with budget 40)
Turn 2 recommends a recipe with no meat, fish, or meat-based stock
Turn 2 gives a full new shopping list and total, not just a recipe name

name: walkthrough
turns: I have chicken, rice and garlic. Suggest one recipe I can make.
Sounds good, let's make it. Walk me through it.
pass_if: get_recipe is called with the recipe_id from turn 1, without the user repeating the recipe name
Turn 2 gives only the first step (or the prep step), not the whole recipe
Turn 3 gives the next step, continuing from turn 2 rather than starting over

name: long_term_memory
conversations: I'm allergic to peanuts and I'm vegetarian. Please remember that for next time.
Suggest one dinner recipe and a shopping list for $25.
pass_if: Conversation 1 calls save_profile with peanuts as an allergy and vegetarian as a dietary restriction
Conversation 2 calls get_profile before anything else, in a fresh thread with no short-term memory of conversation 1
Conversation 2 recommends a recipe with no meat, fish, meat-based stock or peanuts, without the user repeating it
Conversation 2 uses the $25 budget given in that conversation

name: impossible_request
prompt: I have $5 to feed 10 people at a dinner party. What should I buy?
pass_if: The agent says plainly that $5 for 10 people is not realistic
No basket over $5 is presented as fitting the budget
The agent offers a realistic alternative (a higher budget or fewer people) instead of refusing outright
No invented recipes: anything recommended comes from search_recipes
